output.reader_question: What will the SEC's November 9 roundtable discuss, how can the public follow it, and what would still be needed before treating it as a policy signal?
output.editorial_thesis: A concise upcoming-event preview can give readers a concrete way to follow the SEC's discussion of machine-understandable data and Super Intelligence: the announced date, public access and stated focus on use, risks and costs. The useful watchpoint is whether the discussion supplies concrete evidence about those questions. The October 19 announcement itself supplies no policy change, measured benefit, quantified cost or market-reaction evidence.
output.countercase: A roundtable announcement may be only a calendar item. Seeking feedback does not establish an adopted SEC position, impending rulemaking, reliable SI capabilities or a tradable catalyst. Keep this a short factual preview, with the absence of findings doing real work in the argument; do not inflate it into an investment thesis or a broad account of AI regulation.
output.story_kind_reason: This is a narrow preview of an announced public roundtable, not analysis of an economic release or policy decision. It reports the announcement and identifies questions for the forthcoming discussion. No quantitative release, adopted rule or historical series has been admitted. A facts card is the useful visual; quantitative charts would manufacture substance.
